intro: Hi! You already use have/has + the third form for experiences and fresh news (I've been to Bali, I've just finished). Now you'll say how long something has been true with for, since and How long…?, choose between the present perfect and the past simple, and share news like 'I've lost my keys!'. Warm-up: how long have you studied English? Try 'For … years.' or 'Since …'.
teachingNotes: This lesson builds on a2-present-perfect-intro: the form (have/has + third form, I've/she's, haven't/hasn't), ever/never and just/already/yet are known. Recap them in one line only; don't re-teach. New here: duration with for/since and How long…?, the full choice between present perfect and past simple, and recent news. New third forms to give as words to remember: know → knew → known, lose → lost → lost, find → found → found, win → won → won, go up → went up → gone up; had (have) and been (be) are already known.

Duration: the Indonesian trap is 'Saya tinggal di sini sejak 2020' → the node's error *'I live here since 2020' → 'I've lived here since 2020'. Always say why: it started in the past and is still true now, and have/has + third form joins the past and now (the present simple only talks about now). for + a length of time (for three years, for a long time); since + a starting point (since 2020, since Monday, since 8 o'clock). The node's error *'I've worked here since three years' → 'for three years' (three years is a length, not a start). 'Saya sudah tiga tahun kerja di sini' → 'I've worked here for three years', not 'I already work here three years'.

How long + have/has + subject + third form? (*'How long do you work here?' is the trap). Answers: For two years. / Since 2024. 'ago' answers When…?, not How long…? since can take a past simple clause (since I was a child, since I moved to Jakarta). 'last year' alone is a finished time (past simple), but 'since last year' = from last year up to now (present perfect). State verbs work the same: I've known Rina since 2019, We've had our cat for five years, She's been a nurse for ten years (here been is just the third form of be, not 'been to' = pernah ke).

Present perfect vs past simple: a finished time (yesterday, last week, in 2019, … ago, when I was a child, When…?) → past simple; the node's error *'I have seen that film yesterday' → 'I saw that film yesterday'. Up to now (still true) or no time said (experience, news) → present perfect. for goes with both: 'I've lived in Bandung for five years' (still there) vs 'I lived in Bandung for five years' (finished, not there now). Test only with a clear time clue in the sentence.

Recent news: fresh news that matters now, with no time word, uses the present perfect (I've lost my keys! The price of petrol has gone up. Rina has passed her driving test.). News first, details after: the details (when, where, how) are about a finished moment, so they use the past simple even without a time word (I've lost my keys! I think I dropped them on the KRL.). British vs American: Americans often give news in the past simple (I lost my keys!) and say gas for petrol; accept it as American but teach and test the have/has form.

Limits: do NOT teach the present perfect continuous (I've been working here…) — it is a separate lesson; if the learner uses it for duration, accept it as correct but don't explain it. Don't teach still, recently, so far or unfinished time like this week/today, and no past perfect, passive or used to. Keep sentences natural for B1 (work, news, home, Indonesian contexts) and explanations in plain Indonesian.

keyPoints.title: for, since and How long…?
keyPoints.explanation: When something started in the past and is still true now, use have/has + third form, not the present simple: I've lived here since 2020 (not 'I live here since 2020'). for + a length of time (for three years, for a long time). since + a starting point (since 2020, since Monday, since I was a child). Ask with How long + have/has + subject + third form? Answer: For two years. / Since 2024.

keyPoints.title: Present perfect or past simple?
keyPoints.explanation: A finished time (yesterday, last week, in 2019, two years ago, When…?) needs the past simple: I saw that film yesterday (not 'I have seen it yesterday'). Up to now (still true) or no time said → present perfect. for can go with both: I've lived in Bandung for five years (I still live there) / I lived in Bandung for five years (finished, I don't live there now).

id.title: Present perfect atau past simple?
id.explanation: Waktu yang sudah selesai (yesterday, last week, in 2019, two years ago, When…?) perlu past simple: I saw that film yesterday (bukan 'I have seen it yesterday'). Sampai sekarang (masih benar) atau tanpa keterangan waktu → present perfect. for bisa dipakai dengan keduanya: I've lived in Bandung for five years (sampai sekarang masih tinggal di sana) / I lived in Bandung for five years (sudah selesai, sekarang tidak tinggal di sana lagi).

keyPoints.title: Recent news
keyPoints.explanation: Give fresh news that matters now with the present perfect, without a time word: I've lost my keys! (so I can't get in now). The price of petrol has gone up. When you add the details (when, where, how), switch to the past simple: I think I dropped them on the KRL. Americans often say 'I lost my keys!'; this course uses the have/has form.

examples.en: The price of petrol has gone up again.
Good news! Rina has passed her driving test.
examples.id: Kabar baik! Rina lulus ujian SIM.

id.title: Kabar terbaru
id.explanation: Sampaikan kabar baru yang penting sekarang dengan present perfect, tanpa keterangan waktu: I've lost my keys! (jadi sekarang saya tidak bisa masuk). The price of petrol has gone up. Kalau kamu menambah detailnya (kapan, di mana, bagaimana), ganti ke past simple: I think I dropped them on the KRL. Orang Amerika sering bilang 'I lost my keys!'; kursus ini memakai bentuk have/has.

assessment.rubric: Correct: has won (fresh news → has + third form; win → won → won). 'won' = 50 (American past simple; the task asks for the present perfect). 'have won' = 60 (Indonesia = it → has). 'has win' = 40. 'has winned' = 30. 'wins' = 20.

blocks.text:
**Quick recap:** the present perfect is **have/has + third form** (*I've seen, she has finished*). You used it for experiences (ever, never) and fresh news (just, already, yet). Now you use it to say **how long** something has been true.

**The Indonesian trap:** *Saya tinggal di sini sejak 2020* has no tense word, so learners say 'I live here since 2020'. That's wrong. English says **I've lived here since 2020**. Why? The living **started in the past** (2020) and is **still true now**. The present simple (*I live*) only talks about now, and the past simple (*I lived*) only about the past. **have/has + third form** joins the two: from the past **up to now**.

Two small words say how long:
- **for** + a **length of time** (berapa lama?): *for three years, for two weeks, for a long time*.
- **since** + a **starting point** (sejak kapan?): *since 2020, since Monday, since March, since 8 o'clock*.

Indonesian often uses *sudah* here: *Saya sudah tiga tahun kerja di sini* = **I've worked here for three years** (not 'I already work here three years').

id.text:
**Ulasan singkat:** present perfect adalah **have/has + bentuk ketiga** (*I've seen, she has finished*). Kamu sudah memakainya untuk pengalaman (ever, never) dan kabar baru (just, already, yet). Sekarang kamu memakainya untuk mengatakan **sudah berapa lama** sesuatu berlangsung.

**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Saya tinggal di sini sejak 2020* tidak punya penanda waktu di kata kerjanya, jadi pelajar sering bilang 'I live here since 2020'. Itu salah. Bahasa Inggris bilang **I've lived here since 2020**. Kenapa? Tinggalnya **dimulai di masa lalu** (2020) dan **masih benar sampai sekarang**. Present simple (*I live*) hanya bicara tentang sekarang, dan past simple (*I lived*) hanya tentang masa lalu. **have/has + bentuk ketiga** menyambungkan keduanya: dari masa lalu **sampai sekarang**.

Dua kata kecil untuk mengatakan berapa lama:
- **for** + **lamanya waktu** (berapa lama?): *for three years, for two weeks, for a long time*.
- **since** + **titik mulai** (sejak kapan?): *since 2020, since Monday, since March, since 8 o'clock*.

Bahasa Indonesia sering memakai *sudah* di sini: *Saya sudah tiga tahun kerja di sini* = **I've worked here for three years** (bukan 'I already work here three years').

blocks.text: Common mistake: 'I've worked here **since** three years'. Three years is a **length**, not a starting point, so it's **for three years**. Quick test: does it answer *sejak kapan?* (2020, Monday, March) → **since**. Does it answer *berapa lama?* (three years, two weeks) → **for**. And **been** here doesn't mean 'pernah ke': *She has been a nurse for ten years* = she was a nurse ten years ago and she still is one now. **been** is simply the third form of **be**.

id.text: Kesalahan yang sering terjadi: 'I've worked here **since** three years'. Three years adalah **lamanya waktu**, bukan titik mulai, jadi yang benar **for three years**. Tes cepat: apakah menjawab *sejak kapan?* (2020, Monday, March) → **since**. Apakah menjawab *berapa lama?* (three years, two weeks) → **for**. Dan **been** di sini bukan berarti 'pernah ke': *She has been a nurse for ten years* = sepuluh tahun lalu dia sudah jadi perawat dan sekarang masih perawat. **been** hanyalah bentuk ketiga dari **be**.

blocks.prompt: Bu Ani has worked at the bank ___ 2015.
blocks.explain: 2015 is a starting point (sejak kapan?), so since. for needs a length of time (for ten years), and 'from 2015' doesn't say 'up to now' (it needs an end: from 2015 to 2019).

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Bu Ani has worked at the bank ___ 2015.
id.explain: 2015 adalah titik mulai (sejak kapan?), jadi since. for perlu lamanya waktu (for ten years), dan 'from 2015' tidak berarti 'sampai sekarang' (perlu akhirnya: from 2015 to 2019).

blocks.text:
To ask **how long** something has been true, use **How long + have/has + subject + third form?** = *Sudah berapa lama…?* (**subject** = who does it: you, she, Pak Hasan).
- *How long have you worked here?* — **For two years.** / **Since 2024.**
- *How long has Bu Ani been a nurse?* — **For fifteen years.**

**The trap again:** *Sudah berapa lama kamu kerja di sini?* is not 'How long do you work here?' (present simple) but **How long have you worked here?**

**know** and **have** work the same way: *I've **known** Rina since 2019* (kenal; know → knew → **known**), *We've **had** our cat for five years* (punya). *have had* looks strange, but the first **have** is the helper and **had** is the third form of have.

**since + a past simple sentence:** *since I was a child*, *since I moved to Jakarta*. The starting point is a finished moment, so that part is past simple; the main part (up to now) stays present perfect: *I've loved football since I was a child.*

**since last year?** On its own, *last year* is a finished time → past simple (*I moved here last year*). But **since last year** means 'from last year **up to now**', so the verb is present perfect: *She has worked here since last year.*

id.text:
Untuk bertanya **sudah berapa lama** sesuatu berlangsung, pakai **How long + have/has + subjek + bentuk ketiga?** = *Sudah berapa lama…?* (**subjek** = siapa yang melakukan: you, she, Pak Hasan).
- *How long have you worked here?* — **For two years.** / **Since 2024.**
- *How long has Bu Ani been a nurse?* — **For fifteen years.**

**Jebakannya lagi:** *Sudah berapa lama kamu kerja di sini?* bukan 'How long do you work here?' (present simple), tapi **How long have you worked here?**

**know** dan **have** juga sama: *I've **known** Rina since 2019* (kenal; know → knew → **known**), *We've **had** our cat for five years* (punya). *have had* kelihatan aneh, tapi **have** yang pertama adalah kata bantu dan **had** adalah bentuk ketiga dari have.

**since + kalimat past simple:** *since I was a child*, *since I moved to Jakarta*. Titik mulainya adalah saat yang sudah selesai, jadi bagian itu memakai past simple; bagian utamanya (sampai sekarang) tetap present perfect: *I've loved football since I was a child.*

**since last year?** Kalau berdiri sendiri, *last year* adalah waktu yang sudah selesai → past simple (*I moved here last year*). Tapi **since last year** berarti 'dari tahun lalu **sampai sekarang**', jadi kata kerjanya present perfect: *She has worked here since last year.*

blocks.text: Don't answer **How long…?** with *ago*. *For two years* (berapa lama) and *Since 2024* (sejak kapan) answer How long. *Two years ago* answers **When…?** (kapan), and When questions use the past simple: *When did you start? — Two years ago.*

id.text: Jangan jawab **How long…?** dengan *ago*. *For two years* (berapa lama) dan *Since 2024* (sejak kapan) menjawab How long. *Two years ago* menjawab **When…?** (kapan), dan pertanyaan When memakai past simple: *When did you start? — Two years ago.*

material.title: Finished time or up to now?

blocks.text:
You met the basic rule in A2: a finished time → past simple. Here is the full picture.
- **Finished time** → **past simple**: *yesterday, last week, in 2019, two years ago, when I was a child*, and questions with **When…?** *I moved to Jakarta in 2019.*
- **Up to now** (still true: for, since, How long…?) or **no time said** (life experience, fresh news) → **present perfect**: *I've lived in Jakarta since 2019.*

**Careful: for goes with both!** *I've lived in Bandung for five years* = I **still** live there (sampai sekarang). *I lived in Bandung for five years* = that's **finished**, I don't live there now (dulu). Indonesian *Saya tinggal di Bandung lima tahun* can mean either, so English makes you choose: is it still true now?

The same fact, two ways: *I moved here **three years ago*** (when it started → past simple) = *I've lived here **for three years*** (up to now → present perfect).

id.text:
Kamu sudah bertemu aturan dasarnya di A2: waktu yang sudah selesai → past simple. Ini gambaran lengkapnya.
- **Waktu yang sudah selesai** → **past simple**: *yesterday, last week, in 2019, two years ago, when I was a child*, dan pertanyaan dengan **When…?** *I moved to Jakarta in 2019.*
- **Sampai sekarang** (masih benar: for, since, How long…?) atau **tanpa keterangan waktu** (pengalaman hidup, kabar baru) → **present perfect**: *I've lived in Jakarta since 2019.*

**Hati-hati: for bisa dipakai dengan keduanya!** *I've lived in Bandung for five years* = saya **masih** tinggal di sana (sampai sekarang). *I lived in Bandung for five years* = itu **sudah selesai**, sekarang saya tidak tinggal di sana (dulu). *Saya tinggal di Bandung lima tahun* dalam bahasa Indonesia bisa berarti dua-duanya, jadi bahasa Inggris memaksa kamu memilih: apakah masih benar sekarang?

Fakta yang sama, dua cara: *I moved here **three years ago*** (kapan mulainya → past simple) = *I've lived here **for three years*** (sampai sekarang → present perfect).

blocks.text:
A quick test for every sentence:
- Is there a **finished time** (yesterday, last…, in 2019, … ago, When…?)? → **past simple**.
- Is it **still true now** (for or since up to now, How long…?)? → **present perfect**.
- **No time** at all, and it's news or a life experience? → **present perfect**.
The mistake to avoid: 'I have seen that film yesterday' → **I saw that film yesterday**.

id.text:
Tes cepat untuk setiap kalimat:
- Ada **waktu yang sudah selesai** (yesterday, last…, in 2019, … ago, When…?)? → **past simple**.
- **Masih benar sekarang** (for atau since sampai sekarang, How long…?)? → **present perfect**.
- **Tidak ada waktu** sama sekali, dan isinya kabar baru atau pengalaman hidup? → **present perfect**.
Kesalahan yang harus dihindari: 'I have seen that film yesterday' → **I saw that film yesterday**.

blocks.prompt: I ___ to Jakarta in 2019, and I still live here.
blocks.explain: in 2019 is a finished time, and moving happens at one moment, so past simple: moved. The living is still true now (I still live here), but the move itself is finished. 'have moved' can't go with in 2019, and 'move' is the present.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: I ___ to Jakarta in 2019, and I still live here.
id.explain: in 2019 adalah waktu yang sudah selesai, dan pindah terjadi pada satu saat, jadi past simple: moved. Tinggalnya masih benar sekarang (I still live here), tapi pindahnya sudah selesai. 'have moved' tidak bisa dipakai dengan in 2019, dan 'move' adalah bentuk sekarang.

material.title: Recent news: I've lost my keys!

blocks.text:
Indonesian news has no tense: *Kunci saya hilang!* *Harga bensin naik lagi.* In English, **fresh news** that matters **now** uses the **present perfect**, with **no time word**:
- **I've lost my keys!** (so I can't get in now)
- **The price of petrol has gone up.** (it costs more now)
- **Rina has passed her driving test.** (she can drive now)
You hear this all the time on the news: *The government has announced…*, *Prices have gone up…*

**News first, details after.** Tell the news with the present perfect. When you add the **details** (when, where, how), you are talking about a finished moment, so switch to the **past simple**, even without a time word: *I've lost my keys! I think I dropped them on the KRL.*

New third forms to learn by heart: **lose → lost → lost** (kehilangan), **find → found → found** (menemukan), **win → won → won** (menang), **go up → went up → gone up** (naik).

id.text:
Kabar dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak memakai penanda waktu: *Kunci saya hilang!* *Harga bensin naik lagi.* Dalam bahasa Inggris, **kabar baru** yang penting **sekarang** memakai **present perfect**, **tanpa keterangan waktu**:
- **I've lost my keys!** (jadi sekarang saya tidak bisa masuk)
- **The price of petrol has gone up.** (sekarang harganya lebih mahal)
- **Rina has passed her driving test.** (sekarang dia boleh menyetir)
Kamu sering mendengar ini di berita: *The government has announced…*, *Prices have gone up…*

**Kabar dulu, detail kemudian.** Sampaikan kabarnya dengan present perfect. Kalau kamu menambah **detailnya** (kapan, di mana, bagaimana), kamu sedang membicarakan saat yang sudah selesai, jadi ganti ke **past simple**, walaupun tidak ada keterangan waktu: *I've lost my keys! I think I dropped them on the KRL.*

Bentuk ketiga baru yang perlu dihafal: **lose → lost → lost** (kehilangan), **find → found → found** (menemukan), **win → won → won** (menang), **go up → went up → gone up** (naik).

blocks.text: British vs American: Americans often give news in the past simple (*I lost my keys!*) and say **gas** for petrol. Both are understood; in this course we use the have/has form for news. And don't drop the helper: *Kunci saya hilang* is not 'My keys lost' but **I've lost my keys**: *I* lost them, the keys didn't lose anything.

id.text: British vs Amerika: orang Amerika sering menyampaikan kabar dengan past simple (*I lost my keys!*) dan bilang **gas** untuk bensin. Keduanya dimengerti; di kursus ini kita memakai bentuk have/has untuk kabar. Dan jangan buang kata bantunya: *Kunci saya hilang* bukan 'My keys lost', tapi **I've lost my keys**: *saya* yang menghilangkan, bukan kuncinya.

blocks.explain: Fresh news that matters now → has + third form. go up → went up → gone up, so 'has went up' uses the past form. The price = it → has, not have.

id.intro: Hai! Kamu sudah memakai have/has + bentuk ketiga untuk pengalaman dan kabar baru (I've been to Bali, I've just finished). Sekarang kamu belajar mengatakan sudah berapa lama sesuatu berlangsung dengan for, since dan How long…?, memilih antara present perfect dan past simple, dan menyampaikan kabar seperti 'I've lost my keys!'. Pemanasan: sudah berapa lama kamu belajar bahasa Inggris? Coba jawab 'For … years.' atau 'Since …'.
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa 'I've lived here since 2020', bukan 'I live here since 2020'?
Kapan pakai for dan kapan pakai since?
Apakah for bisa dipakai dengan past simple?
Kenapa 'I've lost my keys!', bukan 'I lost my keys!'?

assessment.ppb-1: Lengkapi dengan 'for' atau 'since': Dimas has had his motorbike ___ six years.
assessment.ppb-2: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Inggris: Saya sudah kenal Pak Hasan sejak 2018.
assessment.ppb-3: Tulis pertanyaan dalam bahasa Inggris dengan 'How long' (Sudah berapa lama kamu tinggal di Bandung?): you / live / in Bandung
assessment.ppb-4: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Rina has joined the company in 2021.
assessment.ppb-5: Tulis kata kerjanya dalam bentuk yang benar (present perfect atau past simple): Sari ___ (work) at this hospital since 2019, and she still loves her job.
assessment.ppb-6: Sampaikan kabar ini ke temanmu dalam bahasa Inggris (pakai present perfect): Dompet saya hilang!
assessment.ppb-7: Lengkapi kabar ini dengan present perfect dari 'win': Indonesia ___ a gold medal in badminton!
